Week 38 · Weekend Preview · Sept 18–20, 2026

The Zombie,
The Devotional,
And A Record
That Fell On A Tuesday.

Resident Evil opens day-and-date in India on 96% · Hanuman Ansh dropped 11% in week six · Spider-Man passed Endgame
Boxoffy Desk · Friday 18 September 2026

The best-reviewed video game adaptation ever made opens in four Indian languages today. A ₹2 crore devotional in its seventh week is still the biggest film in the country, and it is falling slower than anything around it. Meanwhile, on an ordinary Tuesday afternoon with no announcement and no re-release, Spider-Man quietly took the biggest record in the business.

The short version

Six things worth knowing this weekend.

Weekend of 18–20 September 2026 · verified figures
Resident Evil released in India on 18 September 2026, day-and-date with the United States, in English, Hindi, Tamil and Telugu. There were no paid previews in India.
Resident Evil holds 96% on Rotten Tomatoes across 121 reviews, making it the best-reviewed video game adaptation ever made, ahead of Werewolves Within at 86%.
Hanuman Ansh has taken ₹243.38 crore India net through day 42 on a ₹2 crore budget. It fell just 11% in week six, to ₹80.25 crore.
Spider-Man: Brand New Day reached $936.77 million domestic on 15 September 2026, passing Avengers: Endgame to become the highest-grossing domestic release of all time.
Mirzapur: The Movie stands at ₹203.20 crore India net after 14 days, having given back 66% in its second week.
Jai Jai Ram, the first song from Ramayana, passed 29 million YouTube views in two days. A.R. Rahman composed it; Arijit Singh and Shreya Ghoshal sing it.
The week that was

One call graded. It landed 9.3% high.

We called Hanuman Ansh's North America opening weekend at $0.85 million. It did $777,824. We were high by $72,176, or 9.3%, on a film that has no comparable anywhere in the market. The other two calls settle over the next fortnight.

And one call moved after publication. We raised Drishyam: The Conclusion from ₹33 Cr to ₹47.5 Cr on opening day. We had ended up below the only forecast anyone has actually printed: Pinkvilla has ₹50–60 Cr, with a ₹57 Cr pinpoint. Our ₹33 Cr leaned too hard on Drishyam 2's ₹15.38 Cr and on the ₹14 Cr Devgn opened Dhamaal 4 to in July. At ₹5 Cr the new band is the tightest we have published. If it misses, it will miss visibly.

A film that took ₹40 lakh in week two dropped only 11% in week six.

Nothing in Indian release holds like that at day 42. Every other holdover on the chart fell between 50% and 84%. Toxic is the mirror image. It opened at ₹101.10 crore, took ₹239.30 crore in week one, and was finished inside nine days. The two sit at ₹243 crore and ₹249 crore, built in opposite directions.

One figure we are flagging rather than printing clean. Mirzapur's week-two number splits by source. Sacnilk's day-wise figures for 11–16 September sum to ₹51.00 Cr. The same page's week-two summary row reads ₹37.75 Cr, a gap of 35%. We have gone with the day-wise sum because it is the granular primary, and the rank holds either way. But at ₹37.75 Cr the drop reads −75%, not −66%.
In cinemas today

Resident Evil opens in four Indian languages.

Sony Pictures India has it out day-and-date with the United States in English, Hindi, Tamil and Telugu, on IMAX and 4DX among other premium formats. Ticketing platforms list it as certified A, running 1h 34m.

It is the best-reviewed video game adaptation ever made. Sony lifted the review embargo on Wednesday, a full two days before release. Studios do that when the scores are the campaign.

A correction, because it is circulating. There were no paid previews in India. Every ticketing platform's date selector started Friday morning, with first shows around 9:15 AM. The Thursday previews being discussed were the US ones, which began at 2 PM local on 17 September. The other 17 September date attached to this film is its Fantastic Fest premiere in Austin. As of publication no US preview figure had been reported.

What India knows, and what it does not

Not much. No CBFC certificate details, no screen count, no advance booking figure and no India opening projection have been published by any Indian trade. Sacnilk's collection page says the data is not available. Bollywood Hungama's shows nothing at all. We are not going to invent a number to cover that.

What we can offer is the band. Hollywood horror in India this year has opened in a narrow lane:

The rest of the Indian slate

Thin. Four small-to-mid Hindi titles: Om Ka Hari, Daayra, Vibe and Bharat Desh Hai Mera. No wide Tamil or Telugu theatrical release at all. Resident Evil is the only new film this weekend with real multiplex pull, so its competition is the holdover stack.

What it has to get past

Hanuman Ansh goes into week seven as the film to beat, and it is the only holdover whose curve is not collapsing. Mirzapur is the exposed one. It gave back 66% in week two, and it now meets Resident Evil in week three with a young male multiplex audience that overlaps almost exactly. Bethlehem Kudumba Unit has run ₹52.30, ₹49.85, ₹33.30 and ₹16.75 crore across four weeks: a decay curve so even it looks modelled.

Projected cume is the verified cumulative through Thursday 17 Sep plus our Friday–Sunday projection. India has no weekday gap — the week closed Thursday and the weekend opens Friday — so these carry no hidden days.

Where we could be wrong. Resident Evil at second is the call with the most air under it. The 2026 India band for Hollywood horror is a ₹1.75–3.30 crore opening day; we are projecting a three-day weekend of ₹9–15 crore, which requires it to run roughly double Evil Dead Burn's pace. The justification is the four-language release, the premium-format footprint and a 96% score. If it opens at Insidious pace instead, it lands fourth, not second.

Domestic

A record fell on a Tuesday.

Before any of this weekend happened, Spider-Man: Brand New Day passed Avengers: Endgame on Tuesday 15 September to become the highest-grossing domestic release of all time, at $936.77 million. It got there in week eight, on a weekday, off an $8.4 million weekend. There was no re-release and no anniversary stunt. It just kept going until the number was gone.

It took the biggest record in the business on a Tuesday, off an $8.4M weekend.

Music

Jai Jai Ram, and a fight about lyrics.

A.R. Rahman's first track from Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana arrived on Ganesh Chaturthi, 14 September. Arijit Singh and Shreya Ghoshal sing it, Dr. Kumar Vishwas wrote the lyrics, and it runs five minutes and twenty seconds over footage of Ranbir Kapoor and Sai Pallavi. It cleared 29 million YouTube views inside roughly two days. The film opens in India on 8 November, Diwali.

The reception was warm, and it was split in a very specific way. Praise went to the composition, the vocals and the visuals. Several outlets noted the track had won over viewers who objected to the casting after the trailer, and that the VFX looked markedly better than earlier footage. Rahman described the intent as keeping the feel of a prayer.

The criticism landed almost entirely on the lyrics. Commenters argued that Vishwas is a fine poet but the wrong choice as a songwriter here. One outlet ran the response as outright mixed, with listeners rating Adipurush's devotional tracks higher. The most common defence was that the lyrics hurt nobody's sentiments, which is an argument about safety and not about quality. That tells you something about the room.

The row that ate the conversation. Hours after the song released, Adipurush lyricist Manoj Muntashir posted his own “Ram Siya Ram” on social media. It was widely read as a dig, and he was dogpiled for it, with users returning his own Adipurush dialogue to him. Within a day the argument had become Ramayana versus Adipurush, and nobody was assessing the song at all.

Why there is no “top 10 of 2026” here. Because no named source publishes one. Spotify Wrapped India, Billboard India's year-end and JioSaavn's annual data all land in December. Luminate's 2026 midyear report carries no India song-level ranking at all. Adding up weekly charts to build a year-to-date list would be reconstruction dressed up as measurement.

The closest published figure is Spotify India's all-time cumulative leaderboard, spanning February 2019 to August 2026 — not 2026. For what it is worth: Alka Yagnik's Agar Tum Saath Ho leads at 651.6M streams, ahead of Arijit Singh's Tujhe Kitna Chahne Lage at 609M. A different chart answering a different question, labelled as such.
Quick answers

The questions people are asking.

Frequently asked · weekend of 18–20 September 2026
When does Resident Evil release in India?
Friday 18 September 2026, day-and-date with the United States, released by Sony Pictures India in English, Hindi, Tamil and Telugu, with IMAX and 4DX among the premium formats. There were no paid previews in India.
What is Resident Evil's Rotten Tomatoes score?
96% across 121 critic reviews, Certified Fresh. It is the best-reviewed video game adaptation ever made, ahead of Werewolves Within's 86% from 2021.
How much has Hanuman Ansh made?
₹243.38 crore India net through day 42, against a ₹2 crore budget. It took ₹80.25 crore in week six, a drop of only 11% on week five — while every other holdover on the chart fell between 50% and 84%.
Is Spider-Man: Brand New Day the highest-grossing film in America?
Yes. It passed Avengers: Endgame on Tuesday 15 September 2026 to reach $936.77 million domestic, making it the highest-grossing domestic release of all time. It did so in week eight, off an $8.4 million weekend.
Who sang Jai Jai Ram from Ramayana?
Arijit Singh and Shreya Ghoshal, composed by A.R. Rahman with lyrics by Dr. Kumar Vishwas. Released 14 September 2026 and past 29 million YouTube views in roughly two days. Ramayana opens in India on 8 November 2026.
What is releasing on OTT this weekend in India?
Lust Stories 3, Irumudi, Modha Rathri and Zakir Khan: Papa Yaar on Netflix; Thudakkam and MobLand Season 2 on JioHotstar; Ram and Leela on Prime Video. All 18 September.

What to watch.

The preview number. Weapons did $5.7 million in previews and opened to $42.5 million. At the same conversion, our $60 million call needed roughly $6.8 million last night. At $8.0 million the top of the band comes into play. The figure lands Friday morning US time, and we will grade against it, not against the talk.

Hanuman Ansh in week seven. An 11% drop at day 42 is not a normal curve, and Resident Evil is an A-certificate horror film competing for almost none of the same audience. Hold once more and it stops being a sleeper story. It becomes the biggest Hindi run of the year.
